entries.title: Shared/Core update: parse-skill

ai.title: Normalize BOM and CRLF line endings in skill frontmatter parsing
ai.summary: The `parseFrontmatter` function in `common/src/util/parse-skill.ts` now strips leading byte-order marks and converts carriage-return/line-feed pairs to Unix line endings before the YAML engine parses the content. This normalization prevents the `yaml` library from retaining carriage returns in the final frontmatter value, a behavior that previously caused skills saved on Windows to fail name validation and be silently dropped during loading. The change ensures that CRLF and BOM variants of a skill document parse identically to their LF-only counterparts.
ai.evidence: In `common/src/util/parse-skill.ts`, the `parseFrontmatter` function now normalizes input by stripping a leading BOM and converting CRLF line endings to LF before passing the string to `gray-matter`, as shown in the hunk replacing `matter(content, MATTER_OPTIONS)` with `matter(content.replace(/^\uFEFF/, '').replace(/\r\n/g, '\n'), MATTER_OPTIONS)`.
ai.unknowns: The diff does not detail the specific Windows user workflow that triggered the discovery of this line-ending mismatch, though a comment references a Discord help request from 2026-11-08.

eli5.text: A small fix now ensures that skill files saved on Windows open correctly in the AI assistant. The software now automatically cleans up invisible formatting marks that Windows adds to text files before reading the details at the top. This prevents the assistant from silently ignoring or rejecting valid skill instructions created on Windows computers.

This change includes two additional updates to the model retirement schedule and the removal of the `freebuffAppDefaultModelIds` export.

Pinned Freebuff Cloud planner and build models to MiMo v2.6 Flash using a new internal constant to isolate them from the new global fallback.

eli5.text: As of November 8, 2026, the default AI model for the free coding assistant is now DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, replacing the previous MiMo v2.6 Flash Fast model across all free and limited access tiers. This means that when you start a new session, the assistant will automatically use the new model, and the old MiMo model is no longer offered as a default choice, though it remains available if you have saved a preference for it. The cloud-based planning and building features are pinned to the previous MiMo model to avoid changing its pricing and data usage terms for those specific tasks.
